topic: The Daily Habit Ep 3: today's 7 stories (Apple's touchscreen MacBook Pro; Cognizant eyes Sarvam stake; Stack Overflow questions crash; OpenAI eyes Google's AI chips; Innodata lays off ~550 in India; Sarvam signs defence AI pact; Chinese AI's hacking test)
angle_hint: An episode digest carousel: slide 1 a bold hook naming the biggest story and that there are 7 stories today; then one stat, compare or fact slide per story for the first five stories in the episode's order (each with its own source); a close slide inviting people to watch the full episode for all of them.

facts.text: Apple's touchscreen MacBook Pro, officially the 'MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display', starts at $2,899 in the US; the 16-inch starts at $3,399.
Pre-orders opened October 28 and first units arrive Friday, November 6. Chips are M5 Pro or M5 Max.
Storage on the new MacBook Pro goes up to 16TB, per The Mac Observer. That article does not give a price for the upgrade.
The Mac Observer lists the 16-inch M5 Max at $4,799 as the highest of the four starting configurations.
Cognizant is reportedly in talks to invest in Sarvam at a $3.5-4 billion valuation, per The Economic Times citing sources.
Sarvam is reportedly seeking about $300 million in fresh capital.
The proposed valuation is more than double the $1.5 billion valuation of its previous round.
In June 2026 Sarvam raised $234 million in the first close of its $300 million Series B at $1.5 billion; HCLTech led with $150 million.
Cognizant could take a small stake; no specific amount is reported.
Stack Overflow got 1,442 new questions in July 2026, 0.7% of its March 2014 peak of 207,204 (a 99.3% drop).
June 2026 had 1,076 questions; July 2026 was higher by 366 questions, an increase of 34%.
Annual questions fell from 1,336,266 in 2022 to 108,981 in 2025.

The figures come from a Stack Exchange Data Explorer query counting questions (PostTypeId 1) by creation month; the query page shows it was created on January 3 (year not stated). Developer Daniel Lockyer published the comparison on X on August 7, 2026.
The plan was first reported by The Information on Oct 27, 2026, citing someone familiar with the matter; no financial terms were disclosed.

In August, Nvidia said OpenAI's current and planned commitments add up to around 12 gigawatts of Nvidia computing, and put the opportunity, including a possible increase to about 16 gigawatts, at about $600 billion through 2030.
Reuters reported in June 2025 that OpenAI had begun renting Google TPUs; OpenAI later said it was only early testing with no plans to deploy at scale.
Oracle said it plans to offer Google's chips on its cloud starting in 2027.
Nvidia closed at $217.94 on Oct 27, about 9% below its Oct 6 record of $239.24.
Innodata has reportedly laid off nearly 550 employees in India, about 5% of its global workforce.
On Monday, October 26, affected employees lost access to company IDs and internal systems during the workday, then got termination emails at their personal email addresses.
The termination email cited a 'ramp-down of the (a) business assignment' and said the decision was not linked to individual performance.
Innodata does data labelling, model training and AI safety testing for clients such as Google, Microsoft and Amazon, and had 10,107 employees globally at end-December 2025.
Job cuts were also reported in the Philippines, and the number of affected employees there has not been confirmed.
Sarvam signed a pact with Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS), under the Defence Ministry, announced 27 October 2026.
Sarvam will build and deploy AI tools for operational, training and decision-support needs of the Army, Navy and Air Force, plus follow-on technical support.
Focus areas include decision support, target acquisition and data fusion, with human oversight retained on operational decisions.
Work will be carried out by Chanakya, Sarvam's firewalled national security and defence division, applying Sarvam's AI stack, including foundation models such as Sarvam 105B.
Search-result summaries of other outlets (YourStory, Angel One headlines) describe it as a five-year agreement; I couldn't open those pages to confirm.

Z.AI's (Zhipu AI) GLM-5.3 completed 3 of 13 multi-stage attack scenarios at least once in controlled simulations, which AI security firm Irregular calls the strongest result it has recorded for an openly available model.

In the tests it gained access to protected services, set up alternative connections to move through networks and coordinated operations across multiple machines. It did not refuse any offensive tasks.

It still trails US models. OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra completed 9 of 10 scenarios in a separate assessment, but the tests were not identical. NIST estimates GLM-5.3 is about four months behind leading US systems.
NIST called GLM-5.3 the most capable open-weight model for cybersecurity tasks released so far.

Anthropic found in September that GLM-5.3 built working attacks against software vulnerabilities in 12% of attempts, versus 14% for its restricted Mythos model. It also found the model's safeguards could be bypassed with fairly simple techniques.

In separate tests Irregular found GLM-5.3 repeatedly reproduced code from memory even when told not to, which it calls 'reward hacking'. The model reached correct answers while breaking the test rules.

cautions: I could not open the Mint article. The $14,549 total, the $7,000 16TB upgrade cost and the ₹ conversions come only from the brief and are unverified.
A search summary attributed the $14,549 maxed-out build (128GB RAM, 16TB, M5 Max, nano-texture) to Tom's Guide. I could not open that page to check it, and no second outlet confirmed it.
The $2,899 and $3,399 starting prices are US prices. I found no India pricing.
Say 'up to' $14,549 for a fully maxed build, not the price of the laptop. Most buyers will pay far less.
The ₹ figures are conversions, and the brief's two figures (₹13.87 lakh and ₹6.67 lakh) differ from the headline's '₹6 lakh'. Use one figure consistently and say 'around'.
Talks only: no deal announced and neither Cognizant nor Sarvam has confirmed.
Based on unnamed sources via ET; valuation, round size and terms could change.
I did not read the ET original; the facts come from Inc42's report of it, so there is no fully independent second source.
Stake size is unreported; don't say Cognizant is buying a big share.
I could not open the Data Explorer query itself (fetch blocked). The facts come from a secondary report, PPC Land, so there is no independent second source for the exact numbers.

The 'fewer than 1,000 a month' framing is not confirmed. The latest full months I found were 1,076 (June 2026) and 1,442 (July 2026). KuCoin gave 1,304 for July, so sources disagree. I found no complete August, September or October figure.
The data excludes deleted posts, so older months are probably understated and the real decline is likely steeper than reported.
